summary:
Charter's newsletter item leads with AI and work signals, then focuses on Clara Shih, a former Salesforce and Meta business AI executive who left Meta this spring to launch the New Work Foundation, a nonprofit addressing the entry-level hiring squeeze.

AI and Work Radar items: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a 3,800-word essay calling for a slowdown in AI capabilities, days after an employee resigned over safety concerns and said Anthropic and OpenAI were gambling with our lives. His three-step plan for pacing the frontier covers third-party evaluators, common safety standards among democratic countries, and coordination with authoritarian governments; executives at OpenAI and Google DeepMind agreed publicly. Challenger, Gray & Christmas data shows AI fell to the fourth-most cited reason for August job cuts after five months at the top, with restructuring and market conditions driving most of the 52,881 cuts. Anthropic also released an interactive tool modeling three scenarios for AI's effect on the US economy by 2030, from internet-sized to railroad-like to a completely transformed economy; GDP and average wages rise in all scenarios while knowledge worker pay stays flat or declines. A Korn Ferry survey of 16,000 professionals found workloads growing despite AI.

Shih says agentic reasoning models shortened product development cycles and reduced team sizes, and she personally removed her team's entry-level job postings or raised experience requirements. Three converging signals pushed her to leave: customers deploying business agents and needing smaller teams, her own team using internal agents for marketing, privacy policy review, sales strategy, product roadmap and prototyping, and young family members facing rescinded offers, silence from employers, and AI-only interviews. The New Work Foundation targets information asymmetry between AI insiders and everyone else through three tools: dearCC media, Field Report hiring and salary data, and Game Plan for job search planning and mentorship. Shih speaks at the Charter Workplace Summit on Oct. 21.
